target_customer: Nigerian freight carriers, truck owners and drivers, then SMEs in supply chains
problem: Freight SMEs must execute orders within 2 to 7 days while invoices can take up to 90 days to pay, creating cash flow gaps and no suitable bank account.
business_model: Neobank fees on payments processed plus interest on capital lent, per TechCrunch
product_category: Business bank account and invoicing for freight carriers

founders.name: Nkiru Amadi-Emina
prior_employers: Kobo360 (enterprise account manager, later head of port operations)
previous_startups: Jalo (2017, on demand delivery platform for e-commerce brands, acquired by Kobo360)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says she founded Pivo in July 2021. Not listed on the YC page, which shows only Akwiwu.

founders.name: Ijeoma Akwiwu
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and COO by TechCrunch; YC page lists her under Former Founders.

exit.reason: Outlets reported the shutdown; founders did not respond to Techpoint requests for comment, so no company stated reason was found.

competitors.name: Duplo
competitors.what: YC backed B2B payments and spend platform for FMCG SMEs in Nigeria
competitors.traction_then: Named by TechCrunch as a potential long term threat if it expanded beyond FMCG

competitors.name: Kobo360 Payfasta
competitors.what: In house payments product from freight logistics platform Kobo360
competitors.traction_then: Cited as an example of e-logistics firms building similar platforms internally

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed a sponsor bank partnership (Providus Bank), debit cards, invoicing and credit scoring for informal carriers, standard fintech integrations but regulated and operationally heavy.

defensibility.rationale: Bank partnership and carrier relationships helped, but TechCrunch notes logistics platforms could build similar products in house.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch in November 2022 saw no noteworthy freight challengers; Pivo shut down in December 2023 and no source shows an incumbent absorbing the wedge.

market_need_then: YC launch page cites 2 to 7 day order execution against up to 90 day invoice payment, with about 500 SME customers reported by TechCrunch in November 2022.

branding.domain_note: Used pivo.africa; the domain later redirected to an unrelated site.
branding.community_and_virality: None found; searches returned only unrelated Pivo brands.

brand_strength.rationale: Regional B2B brand with press coverage of funding but no brand specific evidence.

outcome_analysis: Pivo raised a $2 million seed in November 2022 after a YC backed pre-seed and served about 500 freight SMEs, then shut down in December 2023, about a year later. The founders gave no reason; one commentary notes the lending product relied on outside capital. The cause is not public, so the listed failure factors are inferences from lending economics and the funding climate.
notes: Website fetch redirected to an unrelated domain (pivo.africa to rosas.barcelona), so treated as dead. Techpoint says 550000 dollar pre-seed; Startuplist says 500000, unverified. Techpoint and Ripples name additional leads (Enza Capital, Oikocredit, Partech Africa) that TechCrunch does not; conflict not resolved. Competitor sources are dated November 2022, a few months after the Summer 2022 batch. TechCabal pages were blocked (403) and were not worked around.
